items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I thought McCarthy -- at one time I thought he was the greatest pianist since Art Tatum.

ctx.x: Did people perceive you differently? When you felt you got to that point, did you feel that other musicians recognized something different in your playing?

I didn’t consciously think about that at the time, but looking back, I think probably so. There was a point I was going to make about swing. There was a pianist by the name of James McCarthy who played with Snooky Young’s band. He was from -- I’m not sure if he was from Toledo or somewhere in Ohio, or if he was actually from

Detroit, but I first heard him on the campus at Wilberforce. This McCarthy, he knew every chord change that had ever been invented. To me he sounded somewhat in the Art Tatum family. I was amazed at his technique. I was amazed at his harmonic knowledge. I was amazed at the range and scope of his playing. I thought, wow, this has got to be the greatest piano player that was ever born to woman. This was during my college days. Okay, he played with Snooky Young’s band, and I thought the same thing.
